neighbours.label: ' to' that the word before does not call for as its own complement: 'to' tacked onto a noun, an adjective or a finished clause (a sight to behold, plenty of work to finish, strange to everyone, stood up to sing), whatever follows it, and also after seem / appear / be said / be known ('appears to have'); quiet on 'to' an ordinary verb or fixed phrase asks for (tried / refused / hoped / decided / wants to, gave X to, used to, next to)
neighbours.short: unlicensed ' to' (after noun/adjective/clause or raising verb)
fire: The sunrise over the canyon was a sight to behold.
We still have plenty of work to finish before Friday.
His accent sounded strange to everyone in the village.
She stood up to sing the anthem.
The old bridge appears to have survived the flood.
The author is said to live in a lighthouse.
He seems to know every street in the city.
This is the best place to watch the parade.
quiet: The bakery is right next to the post office.
They decided to paint the kitchen blue.
They tried to behold the sunrise over the canyon.
We refused to finish the work before Friday.
She hoped to sing the anthem.
He gave the old map to the museum.
We used to live near the lighthouse.
The parade passed right next to our house.
